A TabulatedRatingCurve determines outflow from a Basin by looking up the flow rate that corresponds to the current upstream level from a rating curve.
The TabulatedRatingCurve takes a rating curve as input.
Use it for instance to model flow over a weir.

# Tables

## Static

```{julia}
# | code-fold: true
include("../../../utils/gen_docs_table.jl")
table_from_schema(
    Ribasim.Schema.TabulatedRatingCurve.Static;
    restrictions = Dict(:level => "unique", :flow_rate => "start at 0, increasing"),
)
```

### Interpolation

The $Q(h)$ relationship of a tabulated rating curve is defined as a PCHIPInterpolation, for more information see [here](https://www.mathworks.com/help/matlab/ref/pchip.html).

```{julia}
# | code-fold: true
using DataInterpolations
using Plots

level = [12.0, 12.2, 12.5, 13.0]
flow = [0.0, 0.5, 2.5, 8.0]

level_aug = copy(level)
flow_aug = copy(flow)

pushfirst!(level_aug, first(level) - 1.0)
pushfirst!(flow_aug, 0.0)

itp = PCHIPInterpolation(
    flow_aug,
    level_aug;
    extrapolation_right = DataInterpolations.ExtrapolationType.Linear,
)

level_eval = range(first(level), last(level); length = 1000)
flow_eval = itp.(level_eval)

level_extrap_left = [first(level) - 0.3, first(level)]
flow_extrap_left = itp.(level_extrap_left)

level_extrap_right = [last(level), last(level) + 0.3]
flow_extrap_right = itp.(level_extrap_right)

c = :blue
plot(
    level_eval,
    flow_eval;
    c,
    label = "interpolation",
    xticks = false,
    yticks = false,
    left_margin = 5Plots.mm,
)
plot!(level_extrap_left, flow_extrap_left; ls = :dash, c, label = "extrapolation")
plot!(level_extrap_right, flow_extrap_right; ls = :dash, c, label = "")
scatter!(level, flow; c, label = "data", markeralpha = 0.25)
xlabel!("level")
ylabel!("flow")
xlims!(first(level) - 0.2, last(level) + 0.2)
```

Below the lowest given level of 12.0, the flow rate is kept at 0.
Between given levels the flow rate is interpolated using PCHIP interpolation.
Above the maximum given level of 13.0, the flow rate keeps increases linearly according to the slope of the last segment.

For tabulated rating curves with a fixed maximum value (e.g. max capacity of a weir), enter a new row and re-enter the maximum flow_rate at a higher level:

node_id | level  | flow_rate
------- | ------ | ----------
      2 | 12.0   | 0.0
      2 | 12.2   | 0.5
      2 | 12.5   | 2.5
      2 | 13.0   | 8.0
      2 | 13.1   | 8.0

Now this tabulated rating curve node has a flow rate of 8.0 $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$ for all levels 13.0 or higher.

The flow rate is not allowed to decrease with higher levels.
If you wish to e.g. simulate the (partial) closing of a weir when the water level exceeds a certain threshold, you can use an Outlet with a control node to set flow rates.

## Time

This table is the transient form of the `TabulatedRatingCurve` table.
The only difference is that a time column is added.
With this the rating curves can be updated over time.
The `max_downstream_level` currently cannot be updated over time.
Note that a `node_id` can be either in this table or in the static one, but not both.

```{julia}
# | code-fold: true
table_from_schema(
    Ribasim.Schema.TabulatedRatingCurve.Time;
    restrictions = Dict(:level => "unique per time", :flow_rate => "start at 0, increasing per time"),
)
```

# Equations

The TabulatedRatingCurve is a tabulation of a Basin's discharge behavior.
It describes a relationship between the Basin's level and its discharge.
It can be understood as an empirical description of a Basin's properties.
This can include a weir, but also the lumped hydraulic behavior of the upstream channels.

$$
Q = \phi f(h)
$$

Where:

- $h$ is the upstream water level
- $f$ is a function describing the given rating curve $Q(h)$
- $\phi$ is the reduction factor, which smoothly reduces flow from $f(h)$ to $0$ as:
  - The upstream level goes from a water depth of `depth_threshold`, to the Basin bottom;
  - The upstream level goes from `downstream_level + level_difference_threshold` to `downstream_level`, see [Solver settings](/reference/usage.qmd#sec-solver-settings);
  - The downstream level goes from `max_downstream_level - level_difference_threshold` to `max_downstream_level`.

For `depth_threshold`, `level_difference_threshold` see [Solver settings](/reference/usage.qmd#sec-solver-settings).

# Behavior in allocation {#allocation-control}

How a TabulatedRatingCurve behaves in [allocation](/concept/allocation.qmd) depends on `allocation_controlled` in the [Static](#static) table.

A TabulatedRatingCurve that is not allocation-controlled (the default) follows its $Q(h)$ relationship.
Allocation takes this flow into account, but cannot set it directly: it follows from the upstream water level, like in the simulation.

For an allocation-controlled TabulatedRatingCurve, allocation can reduce the flow below what the $Q(h)$ relationship gives, for instance to keep water upstream for a demand there.
Allocation never plans more flow than the rating curve can deliver at the expected upstream level.
The flow rate that allocation sets is used until the next intervention time, set by `intervention_interval` in the [allocation settings](/reference/usage.qmd#sec-allocation-settings), and is in [`allocation_control.nc`](/reference/usage.qmd#sec-results).
The simulated flow in `flow.nc` is the lower of this flow rate and the flow that $Q(h)$ gives at the current level, so it can be lower than what allocation set, for instance when the upstream level dropped, the upstream Basin is almost empty, or `max_downstream_level` is reached.
Since `allocation_controlled` can be given per control state, a [DiscreteControl](/reference/node/discrete-control.qmd) node can switch allocation control on and off.

## Route priority

Usually a TabulatedRatingCurve should follow its $Q(h)$ relationship, and only pass less water when that water is needed for a demand.
This is why TabulatedRatingCurve nodes get a negative [route priority](/concept/allocation.qmd#route-priority) by default, which makes allocation prefer to send water through them.
As long as there is enough water the flow follows the rating curve, and when water is scarce allocation reduces the flow to supply the demands first.

If a TabulatedRatingCurve represents a diversion, a positive route priority makes allocation divert only the water that is needed.
Route priorities are set in the [allocation settings](/reference/usage.qmd#sec-allocation-settings), or per node in the Node table.

For a full worked example, see [Allocation-controlled TabulatedRatingCurve](/getting-started/examples.qmd#allocation-controlled-tabulatedratingcurve) on the examples page.
